text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- State governments finish defending their proposed fiscal budgets for 1997 before federal authorities in capital Abuja, now await broadcast of federal budget.

- Chinese firm charged with reviving Nigerian railways fails to meet deadline of last December to deliver 50 locomotives and 100 wagons; transport minister heads for Beijing to iron out issues concerning the railway contract, officials say.
- Central bank offers six distressed banks for sale to investing public.
- To encourage local entrepreneurs to get involved in Nigeria's vital oil industry, some 20 indigenous oil firms were issued operating licences by end of 1996, investigations show.
- Stock market performance in 1996 showed a rise of 71 percent or 115 billion naira in market capitalisation.
- Home of former head of state retired Major-General Muhammed Buhari in Kaduna, northern Nigeria, looted by bandits who broke in while he was away.
- Nigeria and China sign contract to rehabilitate Port Harcourt quays in southeast and to mechanise coal handling processes at the jetty to facilitate export of the commodity.
- Leaders of Nigeria's five political parties to travel to United States to explain Nigeria's democratisation programme to U.S. interest groups and Nigerian opposition groups abroad.
- Former oil minister Philip Asiodu warns against full divestment by government from oil sector, saying it will amount to mortgaging Nigeria's future to foreigners.
- Defence ministry and other interest groups lobby against scrapping official exchange rate in favour of autonomous rate which is determined by market forces.
